subject: Post-call: Clarify dedicated assurances + hyperscaler comparison (next tests)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@nexthealth.ai>, Tom Brooks <tom.b@nexthealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Clarify dedicated assurances + hyperscaler comparison (next tests)

Hi Alyssa / Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed set of next tests so we can validate dedicated capacity vs the hyperscaler option you mentioned.

High-level takeaways from our convo:
- You want predictable p95 latency under steady traffic and a path for bursty events (triage windows around nightly batch jobs).
- Security/compliance: VPC + audit logs are a hard requirement.
- Budget: order-of-magnitude monthly commitment is likely, but you need capacity guarantees and clear SLA behavior for failover.

Proposed next tests (attached test matrix):
1) Baseline throughput: run your 6-hour synthetic replay at 2048 token context, measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/s on both Redwood Dedicated and the hyperscaler reserved pool. (Owner: NextHealth + Redwood SE)
2) Burst window validation: simulate a spike to 3x normal QPS for 20 minutes, validate autoscale/burst behavior and tail latency. (Owner: Redwood infra + NextHealth infra)
3) Cold-start / rolling upgrade: validate KV cache warm-up and behavior during a rolling model rollout (important for short-lived instances on hyperscaler). (Owner: Redwood SE)
4) Failure and fallback: force a region/fleet outage and validate automatic fallback to pre-approved model variant or lower-cost tier. (Owner: Redwood infra)

Decision criteria we suggest capturing:
- Latency SLAs met: p95 <= 250ms target for interactive routes (you can change).
- Cost delta: total monthly spend for the test workload across scenarios (steady vs burst).
- Operational overhead: manual steps required for scale, rollouts, and audits.

Action items / who’s doing what by when:
- Neha: coordinate schedule and confirm telemetry endpoints by EOD Thu 5/20.
- Karthik: provide optimized config suggestions (batching/quantization) and a quick param sheet by Wed 5/19.
- Marcus: send the reserved vs burst sample cost model and a short note on SLAs by Fri 5/21.
- Alyssa/Tom: confirm a 6-hour replay window and share sample traces/logs by Wed 5/19.

Attachments: Redwood-NextHealth-TestMatrix.xlsx (test cases + telemetry keys), reserved-vs-bursting-cost-model.pdf (sample math).

If that looks good I’ll lock times with Karthik and Marcus.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Re: Post-call: Clarify dedicated assurances + hyperscaler comparison (next tests)

Thanks Neha — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side before we lock tests:

1) On burst behavior: our biggest concern is guaranteed concurrency for live routes during scheduled batch writes (11pm PST). If the hyperscaler uses ephemeral provisioning we need a clear MTTI for extra capacity.
2) For fallback: we need a documented behavior that the model variant used when falling back preserves tokenization and prompt schemas (we can’t accept a variant that changes outputs).

We can commit to a 6-hour replay next Tuesday 5/25 01:00–07:00 PST. I’ll get our infra folks to share traces and an anonymized sample dataset by Fri 5/21.

Also, what's the expected isolation difference between Redwood Dedicated and the hyperscaler reserved instance you referenced? If we commit to reserved GPUs at the hyperscaler we still see noisy-neighbor variability. Any docs you can share would help our SREs.

-Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Director of ML Engineering | NextHealth AI
alyssa@nexthealth.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Clarify dedicated assurances + hyperscaler comparison (next tests)

Alyssa — good points. Short answers and what I’ll add to the test matrix: 

- Isolation & noisy neighbor risk: Redwood Dedicated runs on reserved GPU pools we manage. You get physical capacity isolation at the pool level (we do not colocate hyperscaler tenant workloads on the same pool). Hyperscaler reserved instances reduce preemption risk but still share host-level resources and multi-tenancy characteristics.

- MTTI/MTTR for burst: hyperscalers often rely on provisioning quotas and node boot time (minutes), whereas Redwood Dedicated supports configured burst capacity that’s pre-warmed (seconds) up to an agreed threshold. We’ll include a test that validates your 11pm job behavior specifically.

- Variant compatibility: we’ll lock model hashes for the fallback variants and export tokenizer/metadata in the artifact bundle so the outputs remain consistent.

I’ve updated the test matrix: added concrete telemetry keys (request_id, kv_warm, model_hash), and two dedicated config suggestions:
  * mode: pre-warmed-burst with 10% headroom
  * quantization profile: int8-fast for low-latency interactive routes

I’ll attach a short runbook snippet and a sample config tomorrow.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
